name: Electric Bicycle
description: A two- or three-wheel bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal assist to 20 mph, throttle to 20 mph, or pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts
Class 1: pedal assist only, ceasing at 20 mph; Class 2: may be propelled by the motor alone, with no assistance above 20 mph; Class 3: pedal assist only, ceasing at 28 mph
The motor must disengage when the brakes are applied, and on a Class 1 or Class 3 when the rider stops pedaling
A Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Riders of a Class 2 or Class 3 must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Riders and passengers under 16 must wear a properly fitted and fastened bicycle helmet on any class
Since October 1, 2019, the manufacturer, distributor or seller must permanently affix a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
restrictions.citation: Maine Revised Statutes Title 29-A §2063(14), enacted by Public Law 2019, chapter 349

restrictions.rule: Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match; modified to assist past 20 mph on the motor alone or 28 mph with pedaling, it's no longer an electric bicycle
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Not a motor vehicle, moped or motorized bicycle: no driver's license, registration, plate or insurance
Follows the rules of the road for bicycles, and may use paved shoulders
Class 1 and Class 2 may be ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including bicycle and multi-use paths, unless the municipality or agency that manages a path bans them there
Class 3 is kept off bicycle paths unless the path is within a roadway or the agency that manages it allows Class 3
No class may be ridden on a nonmotorized path with significant natural-surface sections (gravel, stones or wooden bridging) unless the agency that manages it allows it
Private property owners decide whether e-bikes are allowed on their land and private ways
